subject: Post-call: Executive sponsor briefing — growth constraints, procurement path, and escalation items
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Natalie Green <natalie.green@evergrowth.com>
Cc: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.ai>, Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 20 Apr 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: Executive sponsor briefing — growth constraints, procurement path, and escalation items

Hi Natalie — thanks again for taking time today. Quick recap from our exec sponsor call (30 min):

Key business outcomes you described
- Reduce inference cost per session by ~45% to support a planned 3x active user growth this year.
- Maintain 95th percentile latency <300ms for primary user flows (search & compose).
- Avoid model drift on sensitive classification tasks — need deterministic rollbacks and audit logs.

Top pain points we heard
- Current vendor: unpredictable token costs + large token spikes during batch jobs.
- Procurement & security: SOC2 gap for retention/audit; legal needs clear data residency commitment.
- Ops: limited capacity controls causing production throttling during promo spikes.

Proposed approach / next steps (short list)
1) Technical: run a 2-week inference pilot on our Dedicated tier with a constrained traffic profile (we’ll provide a reference config).
2) Commercial: propose a consumption + committed capacity structure (example attached).
3) Security/procurement: introduce our compliance packet and a point-by-point mapping for your SOC2 and data residency questions.
4) Escalation: if procurement needs an SLA exception (latency), we’ll escalate to enterprise sales director.

Action owners & timing
- Marcus: send MAP and performance summary by EOD today (attached).
- Priya (CS): prepare a short pilot runbook and on-call rotation for the trial — draft by Wed 4/22.
- Jasmine (Solutions): map quantization/options best for EverGrowth’s models and expected unit-cost impact — draft by Thu 4/23.
- Natalie: confirm procurement lead + target approval timeline (legal / security) by Tue 4/21.

Attachments: EverGrowth-MAP-v1.xlsx (mutual action plan), redwood-performance-summary.pdf (latency/cost sim)

If that aligns, I’ll loop in our procurement lead and your procurement/security contacts in a single thread tomorrow.

Thanks,
Marcus Lin
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0122

From: Natalie Green <natalie.green@evergrowth.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Renner <tom.renner@evergrowth.com>
Date: Mon, 20 Apr 2026 16:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: Executive sponsor briefing — growth constraints, procurement path, and escalation items

Thanks Marcus — helpful summary. A few quick clarifications from my side: 

1) Procurement lead: Tom Renner (cc’d). Our timeline is tight — we’re aiming for a vendor decision by May 15 with a pilot in market by the end of June.
2) Data residency: we require EU data residency for EU customers; US can be multi-region.
3) Pilot success metric: hit cost-per-session reduction >=35% and P95 latency <350ms under our synthetic load.

I can share our standard security questionnaire (NDA'd) but need your SOC2 + controls mapping to our questionnaire fields before we go too deep.

Tom — can you confirm if procurement/legal need a redline of T&Cs before the pilot?

Natalie Green
SVP Product — EverGrowth
Natalie.Green@evergrowth.com | +1 (312) 555-8872
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Natalie Green <natalie.green@evergrowth.com>, Tom Renner <tom.renner@evergrowth.com>
Cc: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.ai>, Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 20 Apr 2026 18:35:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: Executive sponsor briefing — growth constraints, procurement path, and escalation items

Appreciate the fast reply, Natalie. Quick answers inline: 

- Timeline: May 15 decision target is OK; we can compress internal approval on our side for an early pilot.
- Data residency: we can provision EU-only inference for EU customers on our Private deployment; I’ll include a short note in the MAP about EU residency controls.
- Pilot metric thresholds: we’ll target your success metrics (>=35% cost reduction, P95 <350ms) and instrument with traceable benchmarks.

Procurement: Tom, for the pilot we typically use a short-term MSA + SOW with a pilot fee and committed capacity clause. If you need T&C redlines before pilot start, our legal lead can prioritize — set expectation of 3 business days for a focused pilot MSA review.

I’ve attached a cleaned MAP and an annotated performance summary (two files). Priya and Jasmine are drafting the runbook and quantization notes now — expecting first drafts by mid-week.

If you prefer, I can put together a single procurement/safety packet and propose two pilot contract templates (MSA-lite + pilot SOW) for Tom to review.

Marcus
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.ai

Subject: Pilot runbook + next operational steps (EverGrowth pilot)

Hi Natalie / Tom — following Marcus’ note, attaching the initial pilot runbook draft and a quick ops checklist. Highlights: 

- Pilot scope: 2 weeks on Dedicated capacity (single region), up to 1M tokens/day synthetic traffic.
- Acceptance tests: automated load test (k6), P95 latency measurement, token-cost accounting by endpoint.
- On-call + escalation: Redwood 24/7 on-call during the pilot with named escalation to our enterprise director for SLA exceptions.

Immediate asks from EverGrowth: 
- Confirm procurement contact for signature + whether you need T&C redline prior to pilot.
- Provide a small dataset sample (anonymized) for workload calibration (SFTP link preferred).
